assistant: The upstream OpenClaw gateway holds the Signal conversation, and this repository's door (`apps/assistant`) triages alerts and serves the gateway its tools. On the agenda it reads and writes the team's calendars over CalDAV, makes a Talk call link with `create_video_call` and puts the meeting on each calendar, and sends a Signal reminder with the link before it starts.
caddy: `caddy`, ports 80 and 443, the only container with public ports. It gets its own Let's Encrypt certificates and asks oauth2-proxy about every request to a private subdomain. **Watch out:** it deletes any `Remote-User` header the browser sent, which is why an app can trust that header.
deploy: `harness-auto-deploy.timer`, every two minutes, plus the push webhook, runs `infra/auto-deploy/auto-deploy.sh`. It picks one commit, the gate tests it in its own tree, and only the changed services are rebuilt and must boot. Red or amber ships nothing. The eject ships off.
github: Holds `main`, the issues and the Projects board, and receives the minutes notulen commits. A push to `main` fires the webhook at `deploy.$DOMAIN/hooks/deploy`. The server posts each commit's `vm/gate`, `vm/build`, `vm/boot` and `vm/deploy` status back to its commit page.
gpu: Optional. A Scaleway Kapsule cluster whose GPU pools scale to zero, so a node bills only while it transcribes. Notulen submits a Kubernetes Job; the worker reads the audio from object storage and writes its result to the stack's Postgres, which then listens beyond the server with only its password as guard.
laptop: Claude Code running in this repository, with the harness: skills, guards, overlays and the code index. Every change starts here as one conversation; open this box for the loop it follows. From here the browser reaches the private pages through Caddy, and Signal carries the assistant's questions, pages and briefs both ways. Nothing deploys from your system.
media: Optional: the one node of the media pool role, on its host network, with the flexible IP `MEDIA_PUBLIC_IP` that DNS and Janus name. One pod: the signaling server, the Janus media server on UDP 20000 to 40000, and the Talk recording server, a headless browser that sits in the call. Images built from pinned upstream commits; a CronJob on the system role moves the IP onto a replaced node within a minute. **Watch out:** no TURN relay, so a network that blocks UDP cannot join.
notulen: `notulen` on `notulen.$DOMAIN`, behind the login. Two ways in: a phone recording in five-second chunks, or a recorded Talk call, fetched when the call ends. Either way the audio goes to object storage, is transcribed, and Claude writes the minutes, committed to `NOTULEN_TARGET_REPO`.
observability: Prometheus evaluates its rules every 30 seconds and probes each subdomain over HTTPS; Alertmanager hands a firing group to the alert-relay, and the relay to the assistant. Deadmen run as systemd timers and page straight to Signal when the assistant itself is down. Loopback only: Prometheus on 9090.
sso: `nextcloud` on `cloud.$DOMAIN` with its Postgres, and `oauth2-proxy` on `auth.$DOMAIN`. Accounts live here: Nextcloud is the identity provider, oauth2-proxy the client, and one login with a second factor opens every private name. Files and the calendars the assistant reads and writes over CalDAV live here too.
storage: A Scaleway Object Storage bucket (`S3_BUCKET`) for meeting audio. Notulen uploads the stitched recording before any check that could end the session, so every failed job can be retried. **Watch out:** it keeps billing after the server is deleted.
talk: Talk is the Nextcloud app for chat and video calls, at `cloud.$DOMAIN`. Its calls run through the media node. The recording bot that `infra/media/connect-talk.sh` installs posts every call event of an assistant-made room to notulen, signed with `TALK_BOT_SECRET`.
vault: One Scaleway Secret Manager secret holding the whole environment, secrets included. `infra/secrets/push-env.sh` writes a new version from the laptop; the server pulls it every deploy cycle into `$HARNESS_ROOT/harness.env`, mode 600. A failed pull keeps the old file.
website: `website`, nginx serving the static files in `apps/website/` at the bare domain, public. It links `/design/index.css`, so an edit to `design/tokens.css` restyles it together with the documents and the dashboards.
